title: Through-the-Thickness Pressure Sensors in Spacer Fabrics Using Innovative Spacer Stitching Technology
content: This paper discusses a novel approach of through-the-thickness make pressure sensors by using innovative patented spacer stitching sewing technology for three-dimensional textile structures. Conventional sewing methods compress the material during processing, and the threads are not aligned along the true vertical axis; instead, they adopt a concaved orientation. The uniqueness of spacer stitching lies in its ability to maintain the thread orientation along the vertical axis, enabling a truly rectangular stitch formation. The conductive sewing threads are used as a bobbin thread. They are strategically positioned in vertical axis to realize different thread interlacing point in the thickness of spacer fabric. When the external deformation is applied the tensile stress in conductive sewing thread is changed and so the change in electrical resistance is measured. Cyclic compression tests are performed and spacer fabric are compressed at multiple grades of compression level. The change in electrical resistance is measured in relation to the compression of spacer fabrics. This novel sewing-based approach enables a true single-layer sensing architecture in which the pre-stressed vertical threads themselves act as the sensing element, without collapsing the fabric’s three-dimensional structure.
